ut_creekside_crag.blurb: A small, tucked-away crag beside the stream in Big Cottonwood Canyon, with about eleven routes. Most are traditional lines that take gear, with a few sport climbs mixed in. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up to a single 5.11, and the bulk of the routes sit in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, so it suits climbers moving up from moderates. The walls face south and east, which brings in plenty of sun. Reaching it means dropping down the hill and stepping across the creek, so expect a short scramble before you rope up. Quiet and compact rather than a big destination.

ut_hoss_garden.blurb: A steep, heavily featured wall in Big Cottonwood Canyon, across the road from the Mineral Basin side near the upper-middle part of the canyon. It is mostly a sport crag with a couple of trad lines, about eleven routes in all. Grades start at 5.9 with a few 5.10s, then jump to a solid block of 5.12s and two 5.13s, so it rewards climbers who are comfortable on hard, steep rock. In summer the face is mostly shaded, which helps on hot days, while spring and fall give sunny belays and winter brings full sun. The walk up is a loose scree slog.

ut_red_rock_wall.blurb: A quiet, scenic wall high in Big Cottonwood Canyon, around 8,000 feet up, with views toward the ridgeline above Mineral Fork. About eleven routes, nearly all of them bolted sport lines plus one trad line. Grades run from 5.8 up to a lone 5.11, with most of the climbs at 5.9 and 5.10, so it is a good fit for solid intermediate climbers. The wall faces south. The hike in is steep and the trail can be hard to follow, so expect a real effort to get there, but you are likely to see wildlife before other climbers. Bring a helmet.

ut_reids_peak_ice.blurb: An alpine ice and mixed venue in the Uinta Mountains, at roughly 11,000 feet, on the col's north side between Reids Peak and Bald Mountain. Around eleven routes combine steep ice flows, chimneys and thin mixed climbing. Ice grades cluster at WI4 with one much harder line at WI6, and the mixed routes run from M3 through M6. Several routes are multi-pitch and have a serious, exposed, windy feel, and a few carry an R rating. Some of the more dependable ice in the Uintas forms here, though it swings between lean and fat years, so conditions vary a lot from winter to winter.

ut_ice.blurb: Winter ice around Joe's Valley Reservoir in central Utah, with most of the flows in Straight Canyon or right beside the reservoir. About eleven climbs, almost all water ice plus a single hard mixed line. The ice runs from WI3 through WI5, with the WI4s the most common, so there is something for climbers stepping up as well as those after a steeper pillar. The ice forms against a sandstone backdrop, and conditions can change quickly, so reading the ice and avoiding wet rock matters. Expect post-holing on some approaches when snow is deep, and busy weekends at the best-known flows.

ut_abraxas_wall.blurb: A south-facing sandstone wall in Kane Springs Canyon near Moab, facing the Amasa Back trailhead from across the canyon. It holds about eleven routes, nearly all of them traditional, and the focus is clean one- and two-pitch crack climbing. Grades start at 5.10 and the large majority are in the 5.10 range, with a few 5.11s, so it is a step up from beginner terrain and suits climbers with solid crack skills. Facing south, it bakes in summer but is pleasant on winter mornings. A single sport line sits among the cracks. Wet sandstone is fragile, so wait for the rock to dry fully.
